notice: RN bank batch 143: Pediatric case studies: tetralogy of Fallot, Kawasaki disease, infant heart failure and cardiac catheterization. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that show a hypercyanotic (tet) spell.

rationale.correct: A crying infant with ToF who turns deeply blue with a softer murmur is having a tet spell.

perOption.r3: Less blood crosses the narrowed pulmonary valve.
perOption.r5: Chronic polycythemia, not part of the spell.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of a tet spell.

questions.stem: For each defect of tetralogy of Fallot, indicate its effect.

rows.text: Ventricular septal defect with an overriding aorta
Pulmonary stenosis
Right ventricular hypertrophy

columns.text: Obstructs blood flow to the lungs

rationale.correct: Pulmonary stenosis drives right-to-left shunting through the VSD.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is to {{b1}}, because it {{b2}}.

options.text: place the infant in a knee-to-chest position
lay the infant flat on the back
give a sedative IM before positioning
increases systemic vascular resistance so more blood goes to the lungs

rationale.correct: Knee-to-chest first.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The spell continues. Which orders should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Digoxin IV push to slow the heart rate
Albuterol nebulizer to open the airways

rationale.correct: Oxygen, morphine, fluids and drugs that raise SVR or relax the outflow.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Before surgery, which teaching should the nurse give the parents? Select all that apply.

options.text: Knees to chest and call 911 for a spell
Tell the dentist about the defect
Let the baby cry it out at night to build strength
Withhold all routine vaccines until after the surgery

rationale.correct: Spell plan, hydration, calm care and endocarditis awareness.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: After the spell
exhibits.body: SpO2 back to 84%. Surgery moved earlier.

questions.stem: After complete repair, for each finding, indicate whether it is expected or needs follow-up.

rows.text: SpO2 97% on room air
Pink lips and nail beds
Heart rate 60/min with a new rhythm on the monitor
Feeding well and gaining weight
Chest tube drainage 8 mL/kg in an hour

rationale.correct: Pink and feeding; heart block or bleeding needs follow-up.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that meet the criteria for Kawasaki disease.

rationale.correct: Fever for 5 days with four of five signs is Kawasaki disease.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: For each phase of Kawasaki disease, indicate the typical findings.

rows.text: High fever, red eyes, strawberry tongue
Peeling of fingers and toes, very high platelets
Highest risk of coronary aneurysm
Signs resolve; ESR returns to normal

rationale.correct: Coronary aneurysms are most likely in the subacute phase.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: IVIG 2 g/kg is prescribed. The child weighs 14 kg. How many grams should the nurse prepare? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 2 g x 14 kg = 28 g.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: IVIG 2 g/kg over 10 to 12 hours. Aspirin 80 to 100 mg/kg/day in 4 doses. Echocardiogram.

questions.stem: During the IVIG infusion, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Mix the IVIG with other IV medicines to save lines
Shake the bottle well before hanging it to mix

rationale.correct: Slow start, frequent checks and stop for reactions.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parents, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "We'll wait 11 months for the MMR and chickenpox vaccines."
"If our child is exposed to flu or chickenpox while on aspirin, we'll call."
"We'll keep the echocardiogram appointments."
"We'll give ibuprofen for any fever along with the aspirin."
"The peeling fingers mean the disease is getting worse."

rationale.correct: Vaccine delay, Reye risk and follow-up; avoid ibuprofen with aspirin.

perOption.r5:c1: Peeling is an expected subacute sign.
perOption.r5:c2: Peeling is an expected subacute sign.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
CDC/ACIP immunization schedules

questions.stem: For each defect, indicate the direction of shunting.

rows.text: Ventricular septal defect
Patent ductus arteriosus
Tetralogy of Fallot
Atrial septal defect
Transposition of the great arteries

columns.text: Left to right (more blood to lungs)

rationale.correct: Left-to-right shunts overload the lungs and cause heart failure.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority nursing goal is {{b1}}, using {{b2}}.

options.text: adequate nutrition with less energy use
small frequent feeds with higher-calorie formula and a soft nipple, limiting feeds to 30 minutes
feeding until the bottle is empty however long it takes

questions.stem: Digoxin 10 mcg/kg/day divided twice daily is prescribed. The infant weighs 4 kg. The elixir is 50 mcg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give per dose? Record your answer to one decimal place.

rationale.correct: 10 x 4 = 40 mcg/day; 20 mcg per dose; 20 / 50 = 0.4 mL.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Digoxin 10 mcg/kg/day in 2 doses. Furosemide 1 mg/kg twice daily. Potassium supplement.

questions.stem: Before the morning digoxin dose, the apical pulse is 84/min and the infant vomited twice. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Check the digoxin and potassium levels as ordered
Give the dose and recheck later
Repeat the dose because the infant vomited

rationale.correct: Bradycardia and vomiting suggest digoxin toxicity, worsened by low potassium.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll give digoxin with an oral syringe into the side of the cheek."
"If a dose is vomited, I won't repeat it."
"I'll mix the digoxin in the whole bottle of formula."
"I'll weigh the baby every day on the same scale."
"If I miss a dose by more than 4 hours, I'll double the next one."

rationale.correct: Safe digoxin use and daily weights.

perOption.r3:c1: Dose lost if the bottle is not finished.
perOption.r3:c2: Dose lost if the bottle is not finished.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Highlight the 1-hour findings that need action.

rationale.correct: A cool, pulseless limb after femoral catheterization is an emergency.

questions.stem: For each finding after catheterization, indicate the likely problem.

rows.text: Cool pale foot with a weak pulse
Swelling and spreading blood under the dressing
Irregular heart rate on the monitor
Falling blood pressure with a rising heart rate

rationale.correct: Pulse, site and rhythm checks find complications early.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should {{b1}}, and the child is likely to need {{b2}}.

options.text: elevate the leg and recheck in 2 hours

rationale.correct: Notify and expect heparin.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Which parts of the post-catheterization plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the leg straight for 4 to 6 hours as ordered
Check pulses, color and temperature below the site often
Watch for low blood sugar in young children who were NPO
Let the child sit up and play right away
Remove the pressure dressing at 1 hour

rationale.correct: Leg straight, distal checks, fluids and glucose.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Heparin started. Right foot pulse returned at 3 hours.

questions.stem: The 4-year-old is crying and wants to get out of bed. Which actions fit this child's developmental stage? Select all that apply.

options.text: Offer simple choices, such as which video to watch
Let a parent stay at the bedside
Use a favorite toy or story as distraction
Explain that staying still is a punishment for crying

rationale.correct: Choices, parents and play suit preschoolers.

perOption.d: Preschoolers may see illness as punishment.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.educationalObjective: Take action with developmentally appropriate care.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "No tub baths or swimming for a few days."
"If the site bleeds, I'll press firmly above it and call 911."
"I'll check that the foot is warm and pink."
"A little fever for a week is normal."
"Rough play like the trampoline is fine tomorrow."

rationale.correct: Site care and activity limits.

perOption.r5:c1: Avoid strenuous activity for a few days.
perOption.r5:c2: Avoid strenuous activity for a few days.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
